title: Quickstart dashboards (v1) — wireframe + panel list + alert anti-noise notes
content:
Context
- This is an early wireframe + panel list for the “Quickstart default dashboards” bundle (hosted by the observability-pack repo, but should be importable anywhere).
- Audience: developers running the quickstart templates (RAG / agents / combined) + Redwood internal SRE/DX during launch week.
- Must work out-of-the-box with telemetry contract v1 (OTel traces + metrics + structured logs). Avoid panels that depend on deep internal Redwood-only fields.
- Primary goals:
  1) Help a user answer “Is it working?” in <2 minutes.
  2) Help support/SRE answer “Why is it failing?” without asking for screenshots/log dumps.
  3) Keep alerting defaults quiet (anti-noise) and bias toward “actionable” + “sustained” failures.

Assumptions / inputs
- Templates emit:
  - Trace attrs: request_id, tenant_id (or tenant), environment, service.name, route, model, deployment_mode, region, redwood.route (if using router), error.class, error.code, http.method, http.status_code.
  - Metrics (names tentative; align to telemetry contract v1):
    - http.server.request.duration (histogram)
    - http.server.request.count (counter)
    - redwood.llm.tokens.total (counter) + tokens.input/tokens.output if available
    - redwood.llm.cost.usd (counter) OR derive from token usage + model price (prefer explicit cost metric if shipped)
    - redwood.llm.request.count (counter)
    - redwood.llm.request.duration (histogram) (end-to-end LLM call)
    - redwood.llm.stream.disconnect.count (counter)
    - redwood.llm.error.count (counter) labeled by error.class / error.code
    - redwood.vector.query.duration (histogram)
    - redwood.vector.upsert.duration (histogram)
    - redwood.cache.hit.count / miss.count (counters) (optional)
- We should design with cardinality controls:
  - tenant_id can be high-cardinality; dashboard should allow filtering by tenant but default views should not group-by tenant unless explicitly selected.
  - request_id should NEVER be used as a label in metrics (trace-only).

Dashboard IA (proposed)
Dashboard 0: “Quickstart Overview (Read Me First)”
Dashboard 1: “Service Health (HTTP + Template runtime)”
Dashboard 2: “LLM Calls (Latency, Tokens, Cost, Errors)”
Dashboard 3: “RAG / Retrieval (Vector DB + Chunking)”
Dashboard 4: “Agent / Tools (Tool latency, failures, timeouts)”
Dashboard 5: “Operational (Rate limits / 429s / retries / streaming)”

Note: For v1 ship, we can collapse to 3 dashboards if needed:
- Overview
- LLM + HTTP
- RAG/Agents (conditional panels)

Dashboard 0 — Quickstart Overview (Read Me First)
Purpose: orient + prevent misinterpretation.
Panels (top to bottom)
1) “How to use this dashboard” (text panel)
   - “Start here: select Environment, Service, Template (rag/agents/combined), then look for error spikes.”
   - “If 429s: see Rate Limit panel + recommended backoff.”
   - “If timeouts: check LLM duration p95 + vector query duration.”
2) “What good looks like (baseline)” (text panel)
   - Non-SLO promises, just heuristics:
     - HTTP error rate < 1% sustained
     - 429s rare for low volume; if present, increase backoff / lower concurrency
     - LLM latency varies by model/region; p95 is the key.
3) “Template version / SDK version / commit” (single stat)
   - Prefer from resource attributes: service.version / deployment.version.
   - If not present, omit for v1.
4) “Deep links” (text panel)
   - Link patterns for Redwood Console traces (placeholder, docs to fill in)
   - “Find a trace by request_id: …”

Global filters (applies to all dashboards)
- environment (local|staging|prod) (required)
- service.name (required)
- template (rag|agents|combined) (optional)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private) (optional)
- region (optional)
- model (optional)

Dashboard 1 — Service Health (HTTP + Template runtime)
Time range default: last 1h (toggle to last 24h)
Panels
1) Requests (RPS) by route (timeseries)
   - Metric: http.server.request.count
   - Group by: route
   - Notes: cap number of routes shown (top 10) to avoid noise.
2) Error rate (%) (timeseries)
   - Metric: http.server.request.count filtered http.status_code >= 500 OR error.class != "none"
   - Denominator: total http.server.request.count
   - Target: make this obvious; add annotations for deploys (if service.version changes).
3) Latency p50/p95/p99 (timeseries)
   - Metric: http.server.request.duration
   - Group by: route (optional toggle)
   - Default view: aggregate all routes; drill-down by route.
4) Top error classes (bar / table)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.error.count + app errors combined (if we have one unified metric, use it)
   - Columns: error.class, error.code, count, % of total
   - Example classes:
     - rate_limited (429)
     - timeout
     - upstream_unavailable
     - validation_error
     - tool_error
     - vector_db_error
5) Saturation hints (single stats)
   - Queue depth / worker concurrency (template-specific; may not exist in v1)
   - If not instrumented, omit rather than fake.

Dashboard 2 — LLM Calls (Latency, Tokens, Cost, Errors)
Panels
1) LLM calls per minute (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.request.count
   - Group by: model (optional)
2) LLM end-to-end latency p50/p95 (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.request.duration
   - Split by: model OR route (not both by default)
3) Token volume (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.tokens.total (or input/output)
   - Show total tokens/min; optional stacked: input vs output
   - Anti-noise: do NOT group by tenant_id by default.
4) Cost estimate (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.cost.usd (preferred)
   - If absent: fallback formula note in text panel (“cost not emitted; enable cost metric for Console cost breakdown”).
5) Cost per request (single stat + sparkline)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.cost.usd / redwood.llm.request.count
   - Provide breakdown by model via table (top models by cost).
6) LLM error rate (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.error.count / redwood.llm.request.count
   - Split by: error.class
7) 429s and retries (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.error.count filtered error.class=rate_limited
   - If we have retry.count: show it. If not, show “429 count” and “successful after retry (if instrumented)”.
8) Slow request exemplars (table linking to traces)
   - If the platform supports exemplars: list top N traces by duration with request_id.
   - If not: show instructions: “Open Traces view, filter span.name=redwood.llm.request, sort by duration.”

Dashboard 3 — RAG / Retrieval
Only shown/used for rag + combined templates.
Panels
1) Retrieval query latency p50/p95 (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.vector.query.duration
2) Retrieval error rate (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.vector.error.count (if exists) else derive from logs/trace status
3) Top retrieval collections / namespaces (table)
   - Caution: cardinality risk. If collection names are user-provided and high-cardinality, hide by default.
   - Alternative: show “index/backend” only (e.g., pgvector|pinecone|weaviate).
4) Chunking / ingestion throughput (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.ingest.documents.count, redwood.ingest.chunks.count (if emitted)
   - Otherwise: omit.
5) Cache effectiveness (optional)
   - Metric: redwood.cache.hit.count vs miss.count
   - If we can’t guarantee it across templates, gate behind “if metric exists”.
6) RAG quality proxy (text + link)
   - Not a true quality metric; we can show “context tokens per response” or “retrieval k”.
   - Include link to eval harness runner for real quality regressions.

Dashboard 4 — Agent / Tools
Only shown/used for agents + combined templates.
Panels
1) Tool call volume (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.tool.call.count (if emitted)
   - Group by: tool.name (bounded allow-list)
2) Tool latency p50/p95 (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.tool.call.duration
3) Tool timeouts (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.tool.timeout.count (or tool errors filtered)
4) Tool failure rate by tool (table)
   - Columns: tool.name, error.class, count
   - Ensure tool.name comes from allow-list to keep cardinality bounded.
5) “Guardrails triggered” (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.safety.guardrail.trigger.count (if emitted)
   - Examples: prompt_injection_detected, tool_output_schema_invalid, url_blocked
   - If not in v1, leave as placeholder and do not ship.

Dashboard 5 — Operational (Rate limits / streaming / timeouts)
Panels
1) 429 rate by route/model (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.error.count filtered rate_limited
2) Backoff / retry behavior (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.client.retry.count (if SDK helper emits)
   - If not: add note “Enable SDK retry metric by upgrading to >= X”.
3) Streaming disconnects (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.stream.disconnect.count
   - Split by: client.type (node/python) if emitted
   - Add text: “A few disconnects can be normal on dev networks; alert only if sustained.”
4) Timeout count (timeseries)
   - Metric: redwood.llm.error.count filtered error.class=timeout
   - Include note: “Timeouts can increase with larger docs; tune max_tokens, retrieval_k, and request timeout.”
5) Cold start / startup health (single stat)
   - Use process.uptime + readiness probe failures if instrumented.

Alerting philosophy (anti-noise rules)
- Do NOT ship paging alerts by default. Ship warning-level suggestions + sample rules users can enable.
- Use multi-window burn-rate style alerts where possible to avoid flapping:
  - Example: error budget burn for HTTP 5xx or LLM failures.
- Enforce “for:” durations and minimum traffic thresholds.
- Avoid alerts that depend on low-volume signals (common in dev quickstarts).
- Prefer “ratio” alerts over absolute counts, but include minimum denominator.

Proposed sample alert rules (defaults OFF; included as examples)
1) High HTTP 5xx error rate (actionable)
   - Condition: (5xx / total) > 2% for 10m
   - Anti-noise: only if total_requests >= 200 in same window
   - Severity: warning
2) Sustained LLM request failures
   - Condition: (redwood.llm.error.count / redwood.llm.request.count) > 1% for 15m
   - Anti-noise: min llm_requests >= 100
   - Add label: model (optional) but do not page on model=unknown.
3) Rate limiting indicates concurrency mismatch
   - Condition: 429 ratio > 5% for 10m
   - Anti-noise: min llm_requests >= 100
   - Runbook note: “Reduce concurrency, enable retries/backoff, consider Dedicated capacity.”
4) Streaming disconnect spike (mostly for prod behind proxies)
   - Condition: stream.disconnect.count > 20 for 15m
   - Anti-noise: require stream responses > 200 for 15m (if metric exists)
   - Severity: info/warning only
5) Retrieval latency regression (RAG only)
   - Condition: p95(vector.query.duration) > 2s for 15m
   - Anti-noise: only if retrieval_queries >= 100
   - Runbook note: “Check vector backend health, index size, connection pool.”

Alert noise suppression recommendations (copy for README)
- Use “maintenance windows” / silence during template upgrades and load tests.
- Prefer routing labels: environment=prod only.
- Don’t alert on single tenant by default; use tenant drill-down only during incident.
- If you must alert per route, limit to the top N routes or explicitly defined critical routes.

Wireframe sketch (textual)
- Header row: filters (environment, service, template, region, model)
- Row 1: 3 single-stats
  - RPS (last 5m)
  - Error rate (last 5m)
  - p95 latency (last 5m)
- Row 2: 2 charts
  - Requests over time
  - Error rate over time with deploy annotations
- Row 3: 2 charts
  - HTTP latency p50/p95
  - LLM latency p50/p95
- Row 4: 2 tables
  - Top error classes/codes
  - Top routes by latency contribution
- Row 5 (template-specific):
  - RAG: vector query latency + error rate
  - Agents: tool latency + tool timeouts

Open questions / TODO
- Metric names: confirm final names in telemetry contract v1 (Logan/Allison). We should not ship dashboards that guess at names.
- Cost: do we guarantee redwood.llm.cost.usd for quickstarts? If not, ship cost panels as “optional” and show tokens as primary.
- Deploy annotations: can we rely on service.version changes, or do we need a manual annotation doc?
- Cardinality: confirm whether tenant_id is always present; for self-serve users it might be blank. Ensure dashboards don’t break when attribute missing.
- “Console deep links”: need final URL patterns from Dylan/Console team for linking traces by request_id.

Notes from SRE review (Rafael/Aisha)
- Avoid default alert rules that trigger in local dev (low traffic). Include minimum denominators.
- Prefer error-budget style framing in docs; don’t over-promise SLOs for quickstarts.
- Keep the overview dashboard simple; too many panels makes it harder for first-time users.

Changelog
- 2025-12-06: initial panel brainstorm + IA.
- 2025-12-18: added anti-noise guidance + sample min-traffic thresholds.
- 2026-01-09: added template-specific dashboards (RAG vs Agents) and streaming disconnect panel after SDK discussion.
